🍽️ Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya — the reclining incident and the fear that students will fix the wrong halakha
⚖️ Acting Like Beit Shammai — 'has acted', 'has done nothing', or 'liable to death'?
📜 The Blessings Around Shema — two before, one or two after; long and short formulas

overview.title: 📖 Overview: From Posture to the Blessings of Shema
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 11a–11b
overview.hebrewSource: בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ — פְּרָט לְעוֹסֵק בְּמִצְוָה, וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ — פְּרָט לְחָתָן
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The Gemara finishes the Beit Shammai–Beit Hillel debate over whether one must lie down and stand up for Shema. Beit Shammai read 'when you lie down and when you rise' literally, and use 'when you walk along the way' to exempt a groom and anyone engaged in a mitzva. A story of two sages at a meal, and three Amoraim ranking how bad it is to follow Beit Shammai, close the mishna. A new mishna lists the blessings before and after Shema, and the Gemara fixes their wording: Yotzer Or keeps the word 'darkness' to mention night by day, the second blessing is Ahava Rabba, and a digression settles which Torah study needs a blessing and which formula to use — 'let us say them all'.

slides.title: 🛤️ Who Is Exempt? Reading 'When You Walk Along the Way'
slides.subtitle: Beit Shammai use the verse Beit Hillel relied on to derive exemptions instead

nodes.content: ❓ Beit Shammai: if the verse only meant times, it should say 'morning and evening'. 'When you lie down and when you rise' means actually lying down and rising. So what do they do with 'when you walk along the way'?

📜 Baraita: 'when you sit in your house' — excludes one engaged in a mitzva; 'when you walk along the way' — excludes a groom. Hence: one who marries a virgin is exempt, one who marries a widow is obligated

💡 Rav Pappa: 'like the way' — just as a journey is voluntary (רְשׁוּת), so all who are obligated are on voluntary business. The Gemara refines: בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ — your sitting and your walking obligate; sitting or walking for a mitzva does not

columns.label: Why not a widow's groom?
columns.content: He is not preoccupied (טְרִיד); a virgin's groom is

columns.label: Why not a man whose ship sank?
columns.content: Rav: a mourner is obligated in all mitzvot except tefillin ('bind your splendor upon you', Ezek. 24:17) — so preoccupation alone does not exempt

nodes.content: ✅ The groom is preoccupied with the preoccupation of a mitzva; the ship-owner with a voluntary preoccupation. Beit Hillel agree the verse exempts agents of a mitzva, and derive from it that everyone else recites even along the way

callout.label: Bottom line:
callout.text: Both schools accept that one on a mitzva errand is exempt from Shema; they differ only on whether 'when you lie down' dictates posture.

slides.title: 🍽️ 'Yishmael, My Brother' — A Meal, a Parable, and a Halakhic Worry
slides.subtitle: Two disciples of Beit Hillel switch postures when the time for Shema arrives

lines.speaker: Tosefta
lines.text: Beit Hillel say one may recite standing, sitting, reclining, walking on the way, or even while working. Rabbi Yishmael was reclining at a meal; Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya sat upright. When the time for Shema came, Rabbi Elazar reclined and Rabbi Yishmael sat up.

lines.speaker: R' Elazar
lines.text: A parable: a man is told, 'Your beard is full and suits you.' He answers, 'May it be against those who destroy theirs!' So with you — while I was upright you reclined; now that I reclined, you sat up.

lines.speaker: R' Yishmael
lines.text: I acted according to Beit Hillel; you acted according to Beit Shammai. And furthermore — lest the students see and establish the halakha for generations.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: Why 'and furthermore'? Beit Hillel permit reclining too, so he could have stayed reclined.

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: That applies to one who was already reclining. But to go from upright to reclined just for Shema looks like a ruling for Beit Shammai — so he had to sit up to prevent the students from fixing the wrong halakha.

callout.label: Big idea:
callout.text: A permitted act can become misleading when its timing signals allegiance to a rejected opinion; a teacher must guard what his students infer.

slides.title: ⚖️ Three Amoraim on Following Beit Shammai
slides.subtitle: How wrong is it to recline for Shema like Beit Shammai? Three escalating answers
rows: One who acted like Beit Shammai has acted (עָשָׂה); like Beit Hillel — has acted
Each school agrees the other's practice discharges the obligation
Like Beit Shammai — has done nothing (לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְלוּם)
Sukka: head and body inside, table in the house — Beit Shammai told Rabbi Yoḥanan ben HaḤoranit 'you have never fulfilled sukka in your life'. Each school holds the other's way fulfills nothing
Like Beit Shammai — liable to death (חַיָּיב מִיתָה)
Our mishna: Rabbi Tarfon reclined on the road per Beit Shammai and was endangered by highwaymen; the Sages said 'you deserved to forfeit your life for transgressing the words of Beit Hillel'

callout.label: Note:
callout.text: Beit Hillel cited the sukka visit as proof that Beit Shammai did not object; Beit Shammai retorted that the elders did object explicitly — 'if this has been your custom, you never fulfilled the mitzva of sukka'.

slides.title: 🌅 The Blessings Before Shema — What Exactly Do We Say?
slides.subtitle: Mishna: two blessings before Shema morning and evening; one after in the morning, two after at night

boxes.title: Yotzer Or — light and darkness
items: Rabbi Ya'akov in Rabbi Oshaya's name: based on Isaiah 45:7, יוֹצֵר אוֹר וּבוֹרֵא חֹשֶׁךְ
Why not 'creates brightness'? 'We say it as written' — but the same verse says 'creates evil' and we substitute 'all things'!
Rava: to mention the attribute of night by day and of day by night
Abaye: at night this is 'rolling away light before darkness and darkness before light'

boxes.title: Ahava Rabba — the second blessing
items: Rav Yehuda in Shmuel's name: Ahava Rabba; Rabbi Elazar taught his son Rabbi Pedat the same
Baraita: do not say Ahavat Olam, say Ahava Rabba
The Rabbis say Ahavat Olam, citing 'an eternal love I have loved you' (Jer. 31:3)
Shmuel: one who rose early to study before Shema needs Birkat HaTorah; after Shema he is covered by Ahava Rabba

boxes.title: The Temple's 'single blessing'
items: Mishna in Tamid: the appointed priest said 'recite one blessing'; they read the Ten Commandments, the three Shema paragraphs, then Emet VeYatziv, Avoda, and the priestly blessing
Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Yosei bar Abba could not answer which blessing; nor could Rav Mattana; Rav Yehuda: Shmuel said Ahava Rabba
Rabbi Zerika in the name of Reish Lakish: Yotzer Or — but Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef reports this was only inferred from 'blessings do not prevent one another'

callout.label: Mishna's rule:
callout.text: Where the Sages fixed a long blessing one may not shorten it; a short one may not be lengthened; one may not add or omit a concluding formula.

slides.title: 📚 Birkat HaTorah: What Needs a Blessing, and Which Blessing
slides.subtitle: Four opinions widen the definition of 'Torah', and three formulas compete

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rav Huna: a blessing for Bible only; not for midrash
2️⃣ Rabbi Elazar: for Bible and midrash; not for Mishna
3️⃣ Rabbi Yoḥanan: even for Mishna; not for Talmud
4️⃣ Rava: even for Talmud — Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi saw Rav wash his hands, bless, and only then teach the chapter of Sifra
5️⃣ Which formula? Shmuel: 'Who sanctified us with His mitzvot and commanded us to engage in words of Torah'
6️⃣ Rabbi Yoḥanan adds: הַעֲרֵב נָא — 'make the words of Your Torah sweet in our mouths… Who teaches Torah to His people Israel'
7️⃣ Rav Hamnuna: 'Who chose us from all the peoples and gave us His Torah… Giver of the Torah' — 'the finest of the blessings'
✅ Therefore: לֵימְרִינְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ — let us say them all

callout.label: Takeaway:
callout.text: Each formula praises something distinct — the command, the sweetness, the gift and the choosing — so the Gemara keeps all three rather than choosing one.

summary.principle: Beit Shammai's literal 'lie down and rise' is rejected in practice, and Shema is framed by fixed blessings whose wording — darkness by day, Ahava Rabba, and all the Torah blessings — is deliberately chosen.

flowSteps.content: 🛤️ Beit Shammai: 'when you walk along the way' exempts a groom and anyone on a mitzva errand — preoccupation of a mitzva, not of loss
🍽️ Rabbi Yishmael sits up so students will not fix the halakha like Beit Shammai; Rav Yeḥezkel / Rav Yosef / Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak rank the error
📜 Mishna: two blessings before Shema, one after (morning) or two (evening); long stays long, short stays short

columns.content: 🌅 Yotzer Or keeps 'darkness' — Rava: mention night by day and day by night
💗 Second blessing: Ahava Rabba (Shmuel); Rabbis: Ahavat Olam

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Torah study — even Talmud — requires a blessing, and we recite all three formulas

quiz.q: According to the baraita cited for Beit Shammai, why is one who marries a virgin exempt from Shema while one who marries a widow is obligated?
o: A widow's husband has no mitzva of marriage
The virgin's groom is preoccupied with a mitzva concern; the widow's groom is not preoccupied
The virgin's wedding takes place at night when Shema is recited
One who marries a widow must recite Shema twice
quiz.e: The Gemara answers 'this one is preoccupied (טְרִיד) and this one is not', and then limits the exemption to preoccupation of a mitzva, as opposed to voluntary preoccupation like a sunken ship.

quiz.q: How does the Gemara prove that ordinary preoccupation, such as a ship lost at sea, does not exempt one from Shema?
o: From Rabbi Tarfon, who recited Shema on the road
From the sukka of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben HaḤoranit
From Rav's ruling that a mourner is obligated in all mitzvot except tefillin
From Beit Hillel's rule that one may recite Shema while working
quiz.e: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda in Rav's name: a mourner is obligated in all mitzvot except tefillin (because of 'splendor', Ezekiel 24:17). If a mourner must recite Shema, mere preoccupation cannot exempt anyone.

quiz.q: Why did Rabbi Yishmael add 'and furthermore' when explaining why he sat upright for Shema?
o: Because Beit Hillel forbid reciting Shema while reclining
Because he was worried the students would see a deliberate move to recline and fix the halakha like Beit Shammai for generations
Because reclining is dangerous on the road
Because Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya was his teacher
quiz.e: Beit Hillel permit reclining if one was already reclining. But going from upright to reclined specifically for Shema looks like a ruling for Beit Shammai, so Rabbi Yishmael sat up to prevent the students from drawing that conclusion.

quiz.q: Why does the blessing before Shema say 'creates darkness' rather than the euphemism 'creates brightness'?
o: Because we always recite blessings exactly as the verse is written
Because darkness is created before light in Genesis
Because, as Rava explains, we mention the attribute of night during the day and the attribute of day at night
Because Abaye ruled that 'brightness' is not a Hebrew word
quiz.e: The answer 'as it is written' is rejected since the same verse says 'creates evil' and we substitute 'all things'. Rava explains that darkness is mentioned by day, and at night 'rolling away light before darkness' mentions day (Abaye).

quiz.q: What does the Gemara conclude regarding the several formulas proposed for the blessing over Torah study?
o: Only Rav Hamnuna's blessing, 'the finest of the blessings', should be recited
Shmuel's formula alone, since it matches other mitzva blessings
Each community should choose one formula
Let us recite all of them
quiz.e: After citing Shmuel's formula, Rabbi Yoḥanan's addition of 'make sweet', and Rav Hamnuna's 'Who chose us', the Gemara rules הִלְכָּךְ לֵימְרִינְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ — therefore let us say them all.
